CHOLERA OUTBREAK 2023

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A cholera outbreak claims at least 15 lives. We ask if this was avoidable?

Unique Selling Point:
** NEWS

Summary:
At least 15 people have died as a cholera outbreak rips through the community in Hammanskraal with dozens more hospitalised.

In 2023, surely this should be avoidable. Who's to blame and who will be held responsible to prevent this kind of avoidable tragedy?

Further information:
We recap the situation, breakdown what cholera is and ask the why this was allowed to happen - now in 2023!

INTERVIEWS
Environmental HEalth Expert - John Nyambi
SA Human Rights Commission - Zamatungwa Mbheki
VICTIMS - TBC

Script:


STRUCTURE

OPENING
DRONE SHOT OVER HAMMANSKRAAL… EERIE MUSIC
UPSOUNDS NEWS HEADLINES…. CHOLERA OUTBREAK (3 or 4 clips)

LINK: Water is life, but not in Hammanskraal these last few weeks people. Here it quite literally has meant death for some while dozens of people have fallen ill.

VO: A region of just over 20 thousand people, Hammanskraal is less than 50 km's from our nation's administrative capital.

DIP DOWN TO BLACK

VO: Just over a week ago, Lydia Mashimbye’s sister Martha started feeling sick after work…

LYDIA: When she arrived home she had diarrhoea and started vomiting - it went on the whole night, with no end.

VO: By the Wednesday afternoon, Martha showed no improvement and was rushed to the Jubilee District Hospital - the diagnosis…cholera.

LYDIA: She couldn’t speak and she also wasn’t able to eat.She was very, very weak even with the drip.

VO: It's an infection of the small intestine caused by water-borne bacteria.

LINK: The source of the outbreak has not been confirmed yet, but once cholera starts spreading… it can turn into a death sentence…

JOHN: Cholera is an intricate infection by a bacteria called Vibrio cholerae //with the symptoms of vomiting, fever, diarrhea, stomach cramps.

VO: John Nyambi is a specialist in environmental health.

If left untreated, Cholera can be fatal in a matter of hours.

JOHN: It is dangerous because //when you have fever, you will sweat. So you lose water. When you vomit, you also lose water, when you go to the toilet. And having diarrhea was some type of running stomach. You also lose water so the body runs the risk of dehydration. And then your main organs pick up and then a death follows. 00:00:35:48 - 00:01:52:02

VO: Martha Mobuli died on Tuesday at the age of 47.

LYDIA: – shocking death..

VO: A cholera outbreak on this scale - in this day and age - is unusual. Over 150 people have been hospitalized. At least 22 have died.

ZAMA: This is not the first outbreak. This is not the first outbreak. It's just in this case, we've had so many people dying from it. 00:05:21:42 - 00:05:58:33

VO: It’s a disaster years in the making .

The city of Tshwane’s water crisis has been on the radar of the Human Rights Commission since 2019. In its 2021 report, it found the municipality hadn’t met its constitutional obligation to provide clean water to residents.

Zamatungwa Mbeki is the Commission’s Gauteng Acting Manager.

ZAMA: At this point They can't say that they didn't know. The information that is there, the experts have been saying it for years. They've submitted reports to the city of TSHWANE. We've submitted reports the city of Tshwane, the department, both of these entities know that the water is not fit for consumption. // why is it taking so long?

VO: The people of Hammanskraal are angry and desperate.

UPSOUND CHASING MAYOR CLIP

VO: They chased Tshwane’s Mayor Cilliers Brink from the Jubilee Hospital this week, angry at
bearing the brunt of ineffective governance.

LYDIA: I blame government because they are giving us dirty water // People are dying because of water. I am even afraid to let water touch my mouth, because I’ve seen how my sister died. I am angry because my sister died, because of government, because of water

LINK: Cholera is the canary in the coalmine. If you’re seeing cholera, it’s a symptom of much larger breakdown and decay infrastructure and service delivery

VO: This outbreak is a legacy issue - fuelled by decades of mismanagement and misappropriation of state funds in dysfunctional municipalities.

In 2019, a close to R300 million tender, to upgrade the Rooiwal Wastewater Treatment Plant, was awarded to an allegedly corrupt network with significant political connections. While millions was paid in advance , the project wasn’t completed and the tender cancelled.

ZAMA: And though we might not be able to unpack what actually happened with that process, the result is Rooiwal is not functioning. That is what this means. But as time goes, the reality is that all of these problems with the tenders are far removed from the problems of the people in Hammanskraal.

VO: Currently there are 15 treatment works under the City of Tshwane, but only two are functioning - one is in Hammanskraal and - in that case - barely functioning.

LINK: The Temba Water Treatment Works is functional, but the water that is supplied from here is still NOT fit for human consumption – Hammanskraal residents rely on water tankers to supply potable water.

VO : It’s been this way since long before the cholera outbreak

LYDIA: Even though they are bringing us water in the tankers, it's still the same. She was drinking the water from the tankers, and still got cholera - that means the water was contaminated.

JOHN: In the handling process of that water, in the water, exchanging many hands. Accidents are likely to also occur. // Meaning that an infected person can come into contact and therefore causing infections within the system.

VO: There’s high demand for clean water - and instead of their usual snacks, roadside vendors now sell bottled water.

ZAMA: the state right now says people must boil the water, how are they going to put it with the current state of loadshedding? So all of these things at the end of the day affect poor people. And two weeks from now, two, three weeks from now, the country will have moved on to another scandal. But the people of Hammanskraal are still going to be left with this problem.

VO: The City of Tshwane needs roughly R2.5 billion to effectively turn around the quality of water in the metro - but it’s money Mayor Cillers Brink says they don’t have.

MAYOR: //that is the entirety of the city's capital budget in one single year, // we must admit that the City of Tshwane cannot do this by ourselves, but urgently look at ways of cooperating with the Department of Water Affairs, with private partners in order to get the capital to do those upgrades.

VO: The national Department of Water and Sanitation has previously locked horns with the municipality, but Deputy Minister David Mahlobo, this week hinted at rare cooperation.

DEPUTY MINISTER MAHLOBO; our view that we are going to support them, irrespective of which administration is running the scene, what doing it in KZN in every way while supporting because we can't politicize issues of water, they are about life and death.

VO: 1But action speaks louder than words.

ZAMA: everybody's making commitments now - but they mean nothing if they're not tabled, put in as an action plan and then put with a budget 00:06:25:28 - 00:07:13:48 // without that it's just another broken promise for the people of Hammanskraal. 00:07:18:40 - 00:07:54:28



 
PROMOS:

PROMO 1 - 21 seconds
VO: A cholera outbreak on this scale - in this day and age - is unusual.

ZAMA: This is not the first outbreak. It's just in this case, we've had so many people dying from it.

VO: With at least 22 people dead and more than 150 hospitalized - we ask what’s being done to stop this avoidable infection from spreading.

PROMO 2 - 21 seconds
VO: As the death toll continues to rise in this latest outbreak of cholera - the people of Hammanskraal are angry.

LYDIA: // they are giving us dirty water // People are dying because of water. //I am angry because my sister died, because of government, because of water

VO: It’s a disaster years in the making - that could have been avoided - but who will be held accountable?



PROMO 3 - 21 seconds
VO: It’s a deadly outbreak that was completely preventable

swop 2 bit around
ZAMA: // The information that is there, the experts have been saying it for years // At this point They can't say that they didn't know. 00:00:00:06 - 00:00:28:22

VO: Now government is scrambling to stop the spread of cholera throughout the entire country.
